maya: Quick update from the DDP-13b bring-up: we ran two quant configs on the priming-heavy slice this morning (int4 global vs int6 hybrid). Early signal: int4 saved ~35% token cost but lost ~1.6% recall; int6 saved ~18% cost with ~0.5% recall drop.

sam: Can you post the exact bench numbers (p@k, recall, latencies, sample size)? Also what was the quant impl (per-channel or global)?

maya: numbers: int8 baseline p@k 0.738, int6 0.733, int4 0.722. Recall (longform): int8 0.712, int6 0.707, int4 0.696. Median latency: int8 210ms, int6 195ms, int4 190ms. 95th: int8 520ms, int6 560ms, int4 610ms. Samples: ~5.8k queries on the priming slice (representative traffic). Quant: int4 used q4_0 global scale, no outlier correction; int6 used q6_k with block-wise scales.

noah: Interesting that int6 latency tail increased vs int8. Might be batching differences on the int6 kernels. Also the int4 tail looks worse, probably dequant noise at longer prefixes.

sam: Two follow-ups we should run before routing: 1) int4 with per-channel scale + outlier-correction for embed/attn layers; 2) a traffic-split canary (hybrid selector) that routes only requests with priming_tokens > 400 to int6 for 5% of production for 48h.

maya: Agreed. I prototyped a lightweight selector based on priming_tokens and a tag fallback. Example config I plan to send to GTN: ```{ "selector": { "priming_tokens_gt": 400 }, "policy": { "int6": 0.2, "int4": 0.8 } }```

noah: Please also add expected unit econ delta in the note: show cost per 1M tokens and expected cost delta vs quality loss. Quick calc from our numbers: int8 ~$520/token-µ (use real units below) -> int6 ~18% cheaper, int4 ~35% cheaper. For 1M tokens that's roughly $X_int8, $X_int6, $X_int4.

sam: I'll run the per-channel microbench now. If per-channel recovers >0.7% p@k vs global int4, we can probably avoid routing. Otherwise hybrid looks like a reasonable compromise.

ci-bot: ci: started microbench-perchannel-int4 -> run 3290000020

prod: FYI for GTN: if hybrid routing is proposed we'll need a short product blurb on expected UX regressions and a 2-week rollback plan.

maya: Noted. Action items: sam = per-channel microbench and post stats; noah = help craft the GTN cost/quality summary with 1M token econ; maya = draft routing flag and canary plan. We'll reconvene after microbench results (ETA ~6h).

sam: running now, posting results to this thread when done.

maya: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the single source for the bring-up notes and recommended next steps.
